title: Opentelemetry blog post
description:
Adds a blog post announcing OpenTelemetry support across the R ecosystem.

Scheduled for [2026-02-16].                                                 

The post covers Posit's cross-team effort to instrument Shiny, plumber2, mirai, httr2, ellmer, knitr, testthat, and DBI with OpenTelemetry tracing - enabling production observability with no application code changes.

- Explains what OpenTelemetry is (traces, metrics, logs) and why it matters for R in production
- Lists all instrumented packages with versions and what each traces
- Walks through a concrete example: a Shiny + ellmer + mirai + httr2 weather chat app, with trace screenshots
- Getting started guide (install otel/otelsdk, choose a backend, set env vars)
- Zero-code instrumentation for arbitrary packages via `OTEL_R_INSTRUMENT_PKGS`
- Configuration reference table

@schloerke @atheriel @gaborcsardi you're all listed as co-authors, feel free to comment / push changes directly.

title: mirai 2.6.0 blog post
description:
Release post for mirai 2.6.0.

mirai 2.6.0 brings an HTTP launcher for cloud and Posit Workbench, a C-level dispatcher for near-zero overhead task dispatch, and new tools for racing and debugging async tasks.

Key sections:
                                                                            
- How mirai works — brief intro for new readers, linking to the previous release post for depth                                                    
- Async foundation — positions mirai across the R ecosystem (Shiny, plumber2, purrr, targets, ragnar)
- HTTP launcher — flagship feature; Posit Workbench integration and custom API support
- C-level dispatcher — per-task overhead down to tens of microseconds
- `race_mirai()` — process-as-completed pattern
- Synchronous mode — daemons(sync = TRUE) for interactive debugging
- `everywhere(.min)` — daemon synchronization for remote deployments

title: fix: Avoid putting `<body>` inside `<head>`
description:
Currently, the tidyverse site has some content that _should be_ in the body of the page that's instead being placed in the `<head>` element via the `header.html` partial.

This causes some wonky HTML that's generally resolved by web browsers but introduces semantic errors that make it hard to use tools like `markitdown` to read the contents of the tidyverse blog.

This PR resolves those issues by moving the content from the `header.html` partial to the `baseof.html` partial.

While here, I also wrapped the main content in a `<main>` tag and replaced `div.band` with `nav.band` so that the header links are placed in an appropriate landmark area.

cc @t-kalinowski

title: tidyselect 1.2.0
description:
One thing to be aware of, tidyselect 1.2.0 was supposed to be coordinated with dplyr 1.1.0, but we sent it earlier to ease the release process. This means that some error messages will be suboptimal for users who have upgraded tidyselect until dplyr is released:

```r
# With CRAN dplyr
mtcars |> select(all_of(letters))
#> Error in `select()`:
#> ℹ In argument: `all_of(letters)`.

# With dev dplyr
mtcars |> select(all_of(letters))
#> Error in `select()`:
#> ℹ In argument: `all_of(letters)`.
#> Caused by error in `all_of()`:
#> ! Can't subset elements that don't exist.
#> ✖ Elements `a`, `b`, `c`, `d`, `e`, etc. don't exist.
```

So by posting this blog post we might be encouraging people to update and get the uninformative errors. I have added a note to recommend waiting for that dplyr release in the introduction.

title: WIP: initial draft of 3 article archetypes
description: Hi tidyverse team, Going through this `blogdown` site for some education team projects and thought this addition might make your ["contributing"](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse.org/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) section a bit easier. I added 3 article archetypes, which you can use via the RStudio "New Post" add-in that could make life easier (I hope!): 1. `default.md`- this recapitulates what happens now and preloads the basic post YAML (which is currently populating from the project-level [.Rprofile](https://github.com/tidyverse/tidyverse.org/blob/master/.Rprofile)) - this could be a plain markdown or an RMarkdown post 1. `default-rmarkdown.md`- this should only be used with an R Markdown post and provides only the setup chunk at the top: ```{r setup, include = FALSE} library(testthat) # add / replace as needed knitr::opts_chunk$set( collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.align = 'center', fig.asp = 0.618, # 1 / phi out.width = "700px" ) ``` 1. `package-release.md`- this is the same as the `default-rmarkdown.md` archetype, and should only be used with R Markdown posts, but adds the `usethis::use_tidy_thanks()` code chunk also: ```{r echo = FALSE, eval = FALSE} # to use, set eval = TRUE library(usethis) use_tidy_thanks("OWNER/REPO") ## default: interval = since the last release use_tidy_thanks("OWNER/REPO", from = "2018-05-01") use_tidy_thanks("OWNER/REPO", from = "v1.3.0") ``` I'm not sure if this is useful for you all, or if you already rejected the notion of custom archetypes. But if archetypes are something you may want to integrate, we could work on wording of these, and I could revise the CONTRIBUTING section to reflect using the new post add-in for new articles. Let me know what you think. Alison

title: Add privacy policy for packages that talk to Google APIs
description:
Needed so we can verify the gargle project.

TODOs:

  * [x] Settle on a project / "app" name. Current placeholder in doc is GARGLE_PROJECT. Current OAuth consent screen shows "tidyverse api packages". *I went with "Tidyverse API Packages".*
  * [x] Settle on an email. Currently it goes to "XYZ@rstudio.com" but that should probably change, probably to match the project or "app" name we choose above. *Decision made; alias created.*
  * [ ] ~Determine where to put within the tidyverse.org site and how we are going surface it. Presumably most traffic will come from clicking on a direct link in an OAuth consent screen. But I imagine it has to be *possible* to navigate to it directly.~
  * [x] Once this is merged and has a stable URL, incorporate that link visibly in each package's pkgdown site. *Can't happen in this PR, obviously. But now ... DONE.*
  * [x] Decide if we want the tidyverse logo on our consent screen. *I don't think we have a choice. In any case, I can't figure out how to remove the logo, i.e. without replacing it with another image.*

Background:

  * [OAuth API Verification FAQ](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/9110914)

Key info:

> The Privacy Policy must be visible to users, hosted within the domain of your website, and linked to the OAuth consent screen on the Google API Console.
> The Privacy Policy must be compliant with the [Google API User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy) and the [Limited Use requirements](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy#additional-requirements-for-specific-api-scopes). It must disclose the manner in which your application accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data. Your use of Google user data must be limited to the practices disclosed in your published Privacy Policy.

@hadley I gave another quick read through and found a few more typos:
* can be tremendously _encourage_ 👉 can be tremendously _encouraging_
* You might answer the question, but you'll help someone answer it more easily. 👉 You might _not_ answer the question, but you'll help someone answer it more easily.
* to use in _the every_ data analyses 👉 to use in _the every day_ data analyses (**I'm just guessing this is what you meant, so you may want to double check this sentence**)
* There are a handful _for_ other packages 👉 There are a handful _of_ other packages

I also noticed this small grammatical issue in the packages.md file:
> tibble is a modern re-imaginging of the data frame, keeping what time **has** proven to be effective, and throwing out what **is** not.

I'm not sure if you really care about this change of tense (from has to is) I think it would be proper to state "keeping what time **has** proven to be effective, and throwing out what it **has** not" but that kind of sounds weird 🤷‍♀️. Also probably most people don't care about this level of grammar. ALSO it's possible I'm misremembering my grammar rules. 

Big 🙌 for netlify automagically rendering - I need to switch to that for my casual blogging!
